native_result.query: How did urban land use affect the invasion of different types of introduced plants?
native_result.HypoA: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
native_result.HypoB: Urban land use promoted the invasion of introduced plants through two distinct aspects: the current urbanised habitat gradient (marginal presence OR per +1SD current urban cover: total 2.39***, unintentional 2.23***, gardening 1.49***, agri-forestry ~1.0) and, more independently, the historical expansion of urban land 1956-2009 (full-model OR=1.54**, p=0.006, total; OR=1.37*, p=0.021, unintentional), while effects on abundance among invaded plots were nil. The urban signal acted on whether a plot was invaded, was strongest for unintentionally introduced species (short, predominantly annual, broad-niche weeds, the most successful invaders: 2.1x gardening and 3.7x agri-forestry spread after residence-time control), weaker for gardening (woody/perennial ornamentals), and undetectable for agri-forestry trees; overall urbanisation (above all urban expansion) increased invasion chiefly by favouring the establishment of the unintentional ('weedy') and secondarily the horticultural components of the non-native flora.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded 4 datasets. Plot-level (n=632): nested presence-logistic models per pathway (n.total/n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo): m0 urban-only -> m1 +elevation -> m3 +3 habitat groups + cropland + log(distance.road) + rainfall + longitude, predictors z-scored; abundance part = NegativeBinomial/Poisson on invaded-plots subset. Urban tested as current urban.2009 at 50/500/1000m buffers and Delta-urban 1956-2009 (500m), plus landscape-change categories (50m, ref=no.changes). Species-level (n=81): pathway x trait chi2, Kruskal-Wallis on success metrics, NB of invaded plots ~ pathway (ref=Gardening) + residence time (mrt), family-dummy OLS as phylogenetic proxy. Python 3.12/pandas/numpy/scipy/statsmodels; no internet.

sub_hypo.context: Non-native plant invasion in sampled plots in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening-introduced plants relative to unintentionally introduced plants; no particular land-use year or buffer size is specified.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.

sub_hypo.text: Current urban land cover increased the probability of plant invasion, with a stronger effect for unintentionally introduced species than for gardening species and no detectable effect for agri-forestry species.
sub_hypo.context: 632 plots in Barcelona province; current urban cover measured in 2009 at 50, 500 and 1000 m buffers; predictors standardized.
sub_hypo.relations: Marginal odds ratios for presence per +1 SD current urban cover were 2.39*** overall, 2.23*** for unintentional introductions, 1.49*** for gardening and approximately 1.0 for agri-forestry.

sub_hypo.text: Historical urban expansion from 1956 to 2009 independently promoted overall invasion and invasion by unintentionally introduced plants.
sub_hypo.context: 632 plots in Barcelona province; urban expansion measured at a 500 m buffer in full presence-logistic models controlling for elevation, three habitat groups, cropland, log distance to roads, rainfall and longitude.
sub_hypo.relations: Increasing urban cover between 1956 and 2009 was positively associated with invasion presence: full-model OR=1.54, p=0.006 overall and OR=1.37, p=0.021 for unintentional introductions. The workflow does not specify which cropland buffer was used for adjustment.

sub_hypo.text: Urban land use affected whether plots were invaded but did not affect abundance within invaded plots.
sub_hypo.context: Invaded subset of the 632 Barcelona province plots; abundance assessed using negative-binomial or Poisson models.
sub_hypo.relations: Current urban cover and historical urban expansion had nil effects on abundance conditional on invasion, contrasting with their positive effects on invasion presence.

sub_hypo.text: Introduction pathways distinguished plant traits: unintentional introductions were short, predominantly annual, broad-niche weeds; gardening introductions were woody or perennial ornamentals; agri-forestry introductions were trees.
sub_hypo.context: 81 non-native plant species in Barcelona province; pathway–trait differences assessed at species level.
sub_hypo.relations: Traits differed by introduction pathway as described. The hypothesis does not specify whether broad niche breadth refers to the native or invaded range.

sub_hypo.text: Unintentionally introduced species were the most successful invaders, spreading more extensively than gardening and agri-forestry species after controlling for residence time.
sub_hypo.context: 81 non-native plant species in Barcelona province; negative-binomial modeling of invaded-plot counts by pathway with residence-time adjustment.
sub_hypo.relations: After residence-time control, unintentional introductions had 2.1 times the spread of gardening introductions and 3.7 times the spread of agri-forestry introductions.
